subject: Discovery recap — migrating off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@greenleaf.ai>, Priya Desai <priya@greenleaf.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — migrating off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our conversation and outlined next steps so we have a single source of truth. Let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared
- Cost growth and unpredictability on current proprietary APIs (OpenAI + Anthropic) as usage scales.
- Latency variability across regions impacting interactive features; some requests spike above your 400ms target.
- Vendor lock / commercial terms: want ability to move away from single-provider rate limits and pricing changes.
- Data residency & audit evidence requirements for regulated customers (finance vertical).

Current stack (what you told us)
- Generation and chat: OpenAI (GPT-4o) for customer-facing chat flows; Anthropic for safety-sensitive completions in internal workflows.
- Embeddings: currently using OpenAI embeddings written into Pinecone for vector search.
- Orchestration: internal routing layer (Node.js) that calls APIs; custom prompt templates + logging for fine-tuning QA.

Success criteria for a migration proof-of-concept (POC)
1) Cost: demonstrate >=30% reduction in per-unit inference cost at 95th percentile throughput.
2) Latency: median <200ms and P95 <400ms for the primary chat flows in us-west-2.
3) Quality parity: human-evaluated parity on key tasks (2% tolerance) and automated evaluations (question-answering F1 / retrieval-augmented generation metrics).
4) Compatibility: drop-in compatibility with your current call patterns (streaming, function/tool calling, embeddings vector format for Pinecone).
5) Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence and ability to pin deployments to a private VPC if needed.

Model shortlist & compatibility notes
- Candidate open models to evaluate: Llama 3 chat variants (multiple sizes), Mistral-Chat family (instruct-optimized variants), and Redmond-open variants we’ve tested (quantized 8-bit/4-bit builds).
- Key compatibility gaps we identified: streaming semantics differ slightly (chunking/token framing), function-calling payload formats and stop-token behavior can vary, and embeddings dimensionality differs across providers (we will surface a mapping layer or migration script).

Attachments included
- redwood-compatibility-matrix.xlsx (compatibility notes for generation, streaming, function calling, embeddings)
- SOC2-evidence-request.pdf (list of items you asked for)

Proposed next steps
- Technical deep-dive with your engineering + infra team (1 hour) — propose Tue 10 Mar or Thu 12 Mar. Rishi from our infra team will lead.
- Share mutual action plan and POA (I’ve linked a draft MAP in Drive).
- Run a 4-week POC focusing on core chat flows + embeddings migration; we’ll provide cost and latency baselines.

If that aligns, I’ll lock in the technical call and share a short checklist for a smooth POC kick-off.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the detailed recap — this looks right to me. A few clarifications / requests from our side:

- Cost target: the >=30% reduction is the right ballpark. Can you include a run-rate estimate at three traffic tiers (pilot, 10x, 50x)?
- Embeddings: we currently use Pinecone (vecto index) and have models expecting 1536-dimension vectors. Any change there is non-starter unless you provide a transparent migration strategy.
- Timeline: we’re aiming to start a POC mid-March and have a decision by end of April so business can commit to the Q2 roadmap.
- Security: please confirm what evidence you can provide for data residency in us-west-2 and the typical lead time for Private/VPC deployments.

We’re good to do the technical deep-dive. Tue 10 Mar 10am PT works for our infra lead — Priya will join.

Best,
Liam
Head of Engineering, Greenleaf AI
liam.oconnor@greenleaf.ai
